cands.bio: San Diego County Supervisor for District 5 since 2019. Former San Marcos mayor (2006–2018) and city councilmember (2004–2006). U.S. Navy veteran with an SDSU electrical engineering degree. Delta Air Lines pilot from 1986 to 2020. Ran for U.S. House in California's 48th District.

endorsements.text: Donald Trump and Reform California are listed by Ballotpedia as endorsing his CA-48 campaign.
Incumbent Rep. Darrell Issa, who did not seek re-election, endorsed Desmond for CA-48.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Desmond grew up or when he moved to California. We found no documented positions or actions from him on data centers, new development or land conservation, restrictions on investor or foreign buyers of homes and land, homestead property tax elimination, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. His campaign site states only general goals such as lowering taxes and reducing regulation. We also found no documented controversies, foreign ties, or portrait-quality sources in the pages provided.

cands.bio: San Diego City Councilmember for District 5 since 2020. Earlier worked as a National Labor Relations Board attorney, counsel detailed to the House Education and Labor Committee, and San Diego Deputy City Attorney. Peace Corps volunteer in Botswana. Democrat who won California's 48th Congressional District in 2026.

endorsements.text: The campaign website lists endorsements from the San Diego Police Officers Association, International Association of Fire Fighters Local 145, and Planned Parenthood Action Fund.

Wikipedia lists primary-season support from the California Federation of Labor Unions AFL-CIO, the San Diego and Imperial Counties Labor Council, the California Teachers Association, the LGBTQ+ Victory Fund, Toni Atkins and Rep. Mark Takano.

cands.gaps: We found no record of her positions or actions on data centers, eliminating homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land purchases, H-1B visas, school vouchers or charters, or teacher pay. We found no documented controversies. Her council record on housing, guns and policing comes mostly from her own campaign site, and we could not check it against city records. The campaign site's issues page was cut off partway through. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. We found no independent reporting on her stance toward data centers or large development projects.

local.label: Roots 100: Wikipedia says she was born and raised in San Diego's Scripps Ranch and graduated from Scripps Ranch High School in 2001, and her campaign site says she grew up in North San Diego County. · Money: 6% of money from District 48 ZIP codes after leaving out land and development money (7% before)

qual.background: San Diego City Council member since 2020 (reelected 2024); Deputy City Attorney 2018-2020; NLRB attorney; detail staffer and counsel on the House Education and Labor Committee; Economic Policy Institute associate labor counsel; Fordham JD; law clerk to a federal judge.
qual.why: She holds local elected office and has a legal and prosecutorial background plus congressional committee staff experience on labor legislation, which fits the lawmaking and oversight job.
qual.label: She holds local elected office and has a legal and prosecutorial background plus congressional committee staff experience on labor legislation, which fits the lawmaking and oversight job.

second-amendment.evidence: Her campaign site says she will push for an assault weapons and high-capacity magazine ban, universal background checks, and stronger red flag laws. It also says she wrote a San Diego ban on untraceable ghost guns and won the lawsuit that followed. These are her own claims.

pro-life.evidence: Her campaign site says she will help codify Roe v. Wade into federal law and reverse cuts to Planned Parenthood. It also says she co-authored San Diego's Reproductive Freedom Resolution.

workers-first.evidence: Her campaign site says she opposes ICE tactics and wants to get masked ICE agents off the streets. It says she backs legal pathways to citizenship for long-term residents and Dreamers while keeping borders secure. It also says she led the council effort to join Minneapolis's lawsuit against ICE.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Her campaign site says she will cut red tape and make it easier to build more affordable housing, and that she fast-tracked approval of affordable homes on the council.

back-police-order.evidence: Voted for a 2023 San Diego city ordinance letting police remove homeless encampments from public property when shelter beds were available; it passed 5-4.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Campaign website: she "will cut red tape and make it easier to build more affordable housing to make sure people can live closer to where they work."
